sd.safety.safe.def: Regenerated automatically; removing it costs at most a rebuild or re-download and never loses user data.
sd.safety.review.def: Regenerable, but removal has a visible cost (sign-outs, a multi-GB re-download, lost device symbols, an old backup). Offered, unselected by default, explained.
sd.safety.advisory.def: Reclaimable only through macOS or the owning tool. Shown with its size and the official command; never deleted by us.
sd.safety.never.def: Deleting it breaks macOS, an app or sync, or destroys user data. Always refused.
sd.caches.app.label: App caches
sd.caches.app.why: Cache folders that third-party apps keep under Library/Caches to work faster.
sd.caches.app.regen: Apps rebuild these automatically the next time they run.
sd.caches.app.impact: Apps may start a little slower and re-download some data once. If the app is running, review it before removing.
sd.caches.apple.label: Apple app and system caches
sd.caches.apple.why: Caches kept by Apple apps and background services.
sd.caches.apple.regen: macOS and the apps rebuild them as needed.
sd.caches.apple.impact: Some services download their data again, and apps like Safari lose their warm state until they rebuild it.
sd.caches.container.label: Sandboxed app caches
sd.caches.container.why: Caches inside the private container of an app from the App Store or another sandboxed app.
sd.caches.container.regen: Each app recreates its cache when it needs it.
sd.caches.container.impact: Apps may start slower and re-download data once. From macOS 14, reading other apps' containers needs Full Disk Access, so these are skipped without it.
sd.caches.chromium_apps.label: Electron and Chromium app caches
sd.caches.chromium_apps.why: HTTP, shader and code caches of apps built on Chromium or Electron, such as Slack, VS Code or Discord. A Local State or Preferences file confirms the folder belongs to such an app.
sd.caches.chromium_apps.regen: The app rebuilds these caches on its next launch.
sd.caches.chromium_apps.impact: The app may open slower the first time. Quit the app first.
sd.logs.user.label: App logs and crash reports
sd.logs.user.why: Log files and crash reports that apps write under Library/Logs, including DiagnosticReports.
sd.logs.user.regen: New logs are written as apps run; old ones are not recreated.
sd.logs.user.impact: Only useful when debugging a problem. Removing them should not affect how apps behave.
sd.web.http_storages.label: App cookie and HTTP storage
sd.web.http_storages.why: Per-app cookie and network session storage.
sd.web.http_storages.regen: Apps create it again on next use.
sd.web.http_storages.impact: You will usually be signed out of the affected apps.
sd.web.webkit.label: WebKit website data
sd.web.webkit.why: Local storage, IndexedDB and other website data kept by WebKit-based apps.
sd.web.webkit.regen: Websites and apps create it again as you use them.
sd.web.webkit.impact: Site logins and offline data stored there are lost.
sd.web.safari_favicons.label: Safari favicon cache
sd.web.safari_favicons.why: Small site icons Safari saves so tabs and bookmarks look right.
sd.web.safari_favicons.regen: Safari downloads icons again when you visit the sites.
sd.web.safari_favicons.impact: Icons may be blank for a moment. Needs Full Disk Access to read.
sd.dev.xcode_derived_data.label: Xcode DerivedData
sd.dev.xcode_derived_data.why: Build intermediates and indexes that Xcode produces for your projects.
sd.dev.xcode_derived_data.regen: Xcode regenerates it on the next build.
sd.dev.xcode_derived_data.impact: The next build is slower. Already handled by the Xcode scanner.
sd.dev.xcode_archives.label: Xcode Archives
sd.dev.xcode_archives.why: Archived builds you made for distribution, with their debug symbols (dSYMs).
sd.dev.xcode_archives.regen: Not regenerable unless you rebuild the same source.
sd.dev.xcode_archives.impact: You lose the dSYMs needed to symbolicate crash reports from shipped builds. Already handled by the Xcode scanner.
sd.dev.simulator_caches.label: Simulator caches
sd.dev.simulator_caches.why: Caches Xcode's simulators keep, such as dyld shared caches.
sd.dev.simulator_caches.regen: The simulator rebuilds them on boot.
sd.dev.simulator_caches.impact: The next simulator boot is slower. Already handled by the Simulator scanner.
sd.dev.simulator_devices.label: Simulator devices
sd.dev.simulator_devices.why: One simulated iPhone, iPad or other device with its installed apps and data.
sd.dev.simulator_devices.regen: A new simulator can be created, but the apps and data inside this one cannot.
sd.dev.simulator_devices.impact: The simulator and everything installed in it is removed. Already handled by the Simulator scanner.
sd.dev.npm.label: npm cache
sd.dev.npm.regen: npm downloads packages again when you install them.
sd.dev.npm.impact: The next install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.yarn.label: Yarn cache
sd.dev.yarn.regen: Yarn downloads packages again on the next install.
sd.dev.yarn.impact: The next install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.pnpm.label: pnpm store
sd.dev.pnpm.why: The shared package store used by pnpm.
sd.dev.pnpm.regen: pnpm downloads packages again on the next install.
sd.dev.pnpm.impact: The next install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.brew.label: Homebrew downloads
sd.dev.brew.why: Installers and bottles Homebrew has downloaded.
sd.dev.brew.regen: Homebrew downloads them again when you install or upgrade.
sd.dev.brew.impact: The next install or upgrade needs to download the package again.
sd.dev.cocoapods.label: CocoaPods cache
sd.dev.cocoapods.why: Pod sources and specs CocoaPods downloaded.
sd.dev.cocoapods.regen: CocoaPods downloads them again on the next pod install.
sd.dev.cocoapods.impact: The next pod install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.gradle.label: Gradle caches
sd.dev.gradle.why: Dependencies and build caches Gradle keeps.
sd.dev.gradle.regen: Gradle downloads and rebuilds them as needed.
sd.dev.gradle.impact: The next build is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.pip.label: pip cache
sd.dev.pip.why: Package downloads and wheels pip saved.
sd.dev.pip.regen: pip downloads packages again when you install them.
sd.dev.pip.impact: The next install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.cargo.label: Cargo registry cache
sd.dev.cargo.why: Downloaded crates and their extracted sources.
sd.dev.cargo.regen: Cargo downloads and extracts them again when a build needs them.
sd.dev.cargo.impact: The next build that needs them is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.docker_caches.label: Docker Desktop caches and logs
sd.dev.docker_caches.why: Cache and log files that Docker Desktop keeps outside its virtual disk.
sd.dev.docker_caches.regen: Docker Desktop recreates them as it runs.
sd.dev.docker_caches.impact: Images, containers and volumes are not affected; they live in the virtual disk.
sd.dev.device_support.label: Xcode device support symbols
sd.dev.device_support.why: Debug symbols that Xcode copies from a connected device, one folder per OS version, often 2 to 5 GB each.
sd.dev.device_support.regen: Xcode copies them again the next time a device with that OS version connects.
sd.dev.device_support.impact: Versions for devices you no longer own are pure waste. For a device you still use, the next connection takes a while to copy symbols.
sd.dev.xcode_previews.label: SwiftUI preview simulators
sd.dev.xcode_previews.why: Simulators Xcode uses to render SwiftUI previews.
sd.dev.xcode_previews.regen: Xcode recreates them when you open a preview.
sd.dev.xcode_previews.impact: The first preview afterwards is slow.
sd.dev.xcode_products.label: Xcode build products
sd.dev.xcode_products.why: Built products that Xcode keeps for previews and testing.
sd.dev.xcode_products.impact: The next preview or test run has to rebuild them.
sd.dev.xcode_doc_cache.label: Xcode documentation cache
sd.dev.xcode_doc_cache.why: Documentation Xcode downloaded for offline use.
sd.dev.xcode_doc_cache.regen: Xcode downloads it again when you open the documentation.
sd.dev.xcode_doc_cache.impact: Documentation may be slow or unavailable offline until it is fetched again.
sd.dev.playground_devices.label: Playground simulators
sd.dev.playground_devices.regen: Xcode recreates them when you run a playground.
sd.dev.playground_devices.impact: The first playground run afterwards is slower.
sd.dev.simulator_runtimes.label: Simulator runtimes
sd.dev.simulator_runtimes.why: Simulator runtimes are disk images under /Library/Developer/CoreSimulator, and Xcode tracks them in its own runtime database.
sd.dev.simulator_runtimes.impact: Deleting the files by hand can corrupt Xcode's runtime database, so use the simctl commands shown instead.
sd.dev.android_system_images.label: Android emulator system images
sd.dev.android_system_images.why: Operating system images used by the Android emulator.
sd.dev.android_system_images.regen: Download them again with the SDK Manager.
sd.dev.android_system_images.impact: Each image is a download of roughly 1 to 2 GB, and emulators using it will not start until it is back.
sd.dev.android_avd.label: Android virtual devices
sd.dev.android_avd.why: An Android emulator with its settings and data.
sd.dev.android_avd.regen: You can create a new device, but the data inside this one cannot be recovered.
sd.dev.android_avd.impact: The emulator and the apps and data in it are removed. Quit the emulator first.
sd.dev.go_modcache.label: Go module cache
sd.dev.go_modcache.impact: Go makes these files read-only on purpose, so use Go's own command instead of deleting the files.
sd.dev.uv_cache.label: uv cache
sd.dev.uv_cache.why: Python packages and builds cached by uv.
sd.dev.uv_cache.regen: uv downloads and builds them again when needed.
sd.dev.uv_cache.impact: The next install is slower and needs the network.
sd.dev.precommit_cache.label: pre-commit cache
sd.dev.precommit_cache.why: Environments pre-commit builds for its hooks.
sd.dev.precommit_cache.regen: pre-commit rebuilds them on the next run.
sd.dev.precommit_cache.impact: The next commit that runs hooks is slower.
sd.ai.huggingface.label: Hugging Face models and datasets
sd.ai.huggingface.why: One downloaded model or dataset repository per folder in the Hugging Face cache. Custom HF_HOME locations are not followed.
sd.ai.huggingface.regen: Libraries download them again when a program asks for them.
sd.ai.huggingface.impact: Re-downloading can take tens of GB for large models.
sd.ai.lmstudio.label: LM Studio models
sd.ai.lmstudio.why: One downloaded model per folder in LM Studio's model library. Custom model folders are not followed.
sd.ai.lmstudio.regen: Download the model again from inside LM Studio.
sd.ai.lmstudio.impact: Large downloads; the model is unavailable until it is fetched again. Quit LM Studio first.
sd.ai.torch_hub.label: PyTorch Hub downloads
sd.ai.torch_hub.why: Models and code that torch.hub downloaded.
sd.ai.torch_hub.regen: PyTorch downloads them again when a program asks for them.
sd.ai.torch_hub.impact: Programs that rely on them will download them again, which can be large.
sd.ai.whisper.label: Whisper model weights
sd.ai.whisper.why: Speech-recognition model files downloaded by Whisper.
sd.ai.whisper.regen: Whisper downloads the model again when you use it.
sd.ai.whisper.impact: The next transcription waits for the model to download again.
sd.ai.ollama.label: Ollama models
sd.ai.ollama.why: Models you pulled with Ollama. Models share data blocks through manifests.
sd.ai.ollama.impact: Deleting files by hand can break other models that share the same data. Use ollama's own commands.
sd.ai.apple_intelligence.label: Apple Intelligence models
sd.ai.apple_intelligence.why: On-device models that macOS manages in system storage when Apple Intelligence is on. Which macOS versions have them is not fully verified here.
sd.ai.apple_intelligence.impact: To release the space, turn Apple Intelligence off in System Settings. We may not be able to measure the size without administrator access.
sd.backups.ios.label: iPhone and iPad backups
sd.backups.ios.why: A full backup of an iPhone or iPad made through Finder. The description shows the device name and the last backup date.
sd.backups.ios.regen: A new backup can be made while the device is connected, but this one cannot be recreated.
sd.backups.ios.impact: If it is the only backup of that device, emptying the Trash loses it for good. Needs Full Disk Access to read.
sd.backups.ipsw.label: iOS and iPadOS installers
sd.backups.ipsw.why: Software update files (.ipsw) that Finder downloaded to update or restore a device.
sd.backups.ipsw.regen: Finder downloads the file again when you need it.
sd.backups.ipsw.impact: Updating or restoring a device will download the installer again.
sd.snapshots.tm_local.label: Time Machine local snapshots
sd.snapshots.tm_local.why: APFS local snapshots that Time Machine keeps on this Mac.
sd.snapshots.tm_local.impact: macOS deletes them on its own as they age or when space is needed; this is shown so you can understand the number. The delete command may require administrator rights.
sd.vm.docker_raw.label: Docker Desktop disk
sd.vm.docker_raw.why: The single disk file that holds every Docker image, container and volume. The size shown is the space actually allocated, since the file is sparse.
sd.vm.docker_raw.impact: Moving it to the Trash destroys all images, containers and volumes. Use docker's own commands to free space.
sd.vm.colima.label: Colima virtual machines
sd.vm.colima.why: The disks and configuration of Colima's virtual machines.
sd.vm.colima.impact: Deleting files by hand breaks the VM. Use colima's own commands.
sd.mail.downloads.label: Mail attachment copies
sd.mail.downloads.why: Copies of attachments you opened from Mail.
sd.mail.downloads.regen: Mail downloads the attachment again from the mailbox when you open it.
sd.mail.downloads.impact: The originals stay in your mailbox. Needs Full Disk Access to read; quit Mail first.
sd.messages.attachments.label: Messages attachments
sd.messages.attachments.why: Photos, videos and files from your conversations in Messages. This is your data, so it is only measured.
sd.messages.attachments.impact: To free space, use Messages Settings (Keep messages) or Storage settings, which manage it safely.
sd.sys.var_folders.label: Per-user temp and cache folders
sd.sys.var_folders.why: Temporary and cache data that macOS keeps under /private/var/folders for your user. Running apps use it.
sd.sys.var_folders.impact: Restarting your Mac is the safe way to clear it; we only show its size.
sd.never.cloud_files.label: Cloud storage files
sd.never.cloud_files.why: iCloud Drive and file-provider data from services like Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive. Removing it can delete the only local copy of your files or cause sync conflicts.
sd.never.identity_sync.label: Account and sync state
sd.never.identity_sync.why: Folders under Caches that hold account, iCloud sync, Wallet and Home state, despite their location. Removing them can sign you out, force a full resync or break Wallet and Home.
sd.never.in_flight.label: Active downloads and open documents
sd.never.in_flight.why: Background downloads in progress and documents that are open or autosaved. Removing them can lose unsaved work or abort a download.
sd.never.personal_data.label: Personal data and settings
sd.never.personal_data.why: Messages, Mail, Photos, Calendars, Contacts, Keychains, Cookies, Accounts and Preferences. This is your data and your settings, not a cache.
sd.never.group_containers.label: App group containers
sd.never.group_containers.why: State shared between an app and its extensions, and protected by macOS from version 15. Removing it can break apps and their extensions.
sd.never.vm_internals.label: VM and model store internals
sd.never.vm_internals.why: Docker's virtual disk, Colima VMs and Ollama's shared blobs and manifests. These are managed by their own tools, and deleting files by hand can destroy data or break other models.
sd.never.roots.label: Container folders
sd.never.roots.why: Parent folders such as Library, Caches and Application Support. Only their children can be offered, one at a time; a parent is never an item itself.
sd.never.os.label: macOS system files
sd.never.os.why: System files, kernel extensions, system libraries, swap and sleep image, the Spotlight index, OS assets, updates and simulator runtime images. Removing them can make the Mac fail to start, break updates or corrupt Xcode.
